study_identification_part.si4_title: Personalizing progressive changes to brain structure in Alzheimer's disease using normative modeling

cm1_research_objectives.reason: The paper clearly states the objectives and the purpose of applying normative modeling. It aims to: (1) track disease trajectories in MCI and AD using individualized z-score maps, (2) predict progression from MCI to AD, and (3) relate normative modeling markers to other AD markers. This satisfies both criteria: research questions are provided and the purpose of applying normative modeling is explicitly described.
cm1_research_objectives.supporting_text: "Here we used normative modeling to track individuals' disease progression in people with mild cognitive impairment (MCI) and patients with AD." … "We assess whether markers of regional brain atrophy derived from normative modeling (1) can track disease trajectories in people with MCI and patients with AD; (2) can be used to predict progression from MCI to AD; and (3) are related to other common imaging and non-imaging AD markers."

nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.reason: This study uses an EXISTING normative model trained on healthy controls from multiple public datasets with prior publications cited. Transfer learning/recalibration is performed using 70% of cognitively unimpaired ADNI controls per site; image quality standards are described (FreeSurfer QC and ADNI raw scan QC); the final sample size and dataset composition are reported. These satisfy the criteria for studies using an existing model (citation of original reference cohort and description of local calibration sample and QC, plus final N).
nm1_selection_criteria_reference_cohort.supporting_text: "The reference dataset was made by combining T1-weighted MRI scan data on healthy people from multiple publicly available sources… totaling 58,836 individuals from 82 sites. Data collection, data processing, and participant demographics of the reference dataset were described previously." … "This model was trained on 58,836 scans… using the covariates age, sex, and site… Next, these estimates were calibrated to our specific test data (i.e., ADNI), using an adapted transfer learning approach… using 70% of cognitively unimpaired controls per ADNI site…" … "For the research dataset, quality control was based on a visual review of each cortical region…" … "The final sample used in z score analysis is n = 1181, which included 3233 scans."
